item.title: Iran’s new ambassador to Greece meets with FM Araghchi
item.description: Mahmoud Heidari, the new ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Greece, met with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi before departing for his diplomatic mission. During the meeting, the new ambassador outlined his proposed plan for Tehran–Athens relations and for utilizing existing capacities to expand cooperation in various fields. The foreign minister wished the new ambassador success in his mission and, referring to the historical background of relations between Iran and Greece as two ancient civilizations, stressed the need to pursue and strengthen relations between the Islamic Republic of Iran and Greece within the framework of agreements and cooperation documents between the two countries. Before being appointed as Iran’s ambassador to Greece, Mahmoud Heidari served as an assistant to the foreign minister and director general for Mediterranean and Eastern European affairs at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Iranian Jordanian FMs hold phone talks discuss regional developments
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi held a phone conversation on Tuesday morning to discuss regional developments. During the conversation, Araghchi outlined Iran’s positions on regional developments and stressed the need for Islamic countries and the international community to take serious action to counter the continued genocide and expansionism of the occupying Zionist regime. Recalling the devastating consequences of the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran for the region and the world, the Iranian foreign minister emphasized that restoring security to the region requires an end to the United States’ aggressive and interventionist actions, as well as containing the Zionist regime’s expansionism and warmongering. Araghchi also condemned the terrorist attack on a church in southern Jordan and expressed his condolences to the families of those killed in the incident. The foreign ministers of the two countries underscored the importance of making use of diplomacy and continuing political consultations to safeguard peace and stability in the region.

item.title: Iran’s new ambassador to Uganda meets Foreign Minister Araghchi
item.description: Reza Nourian, the newly appointed ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Uganda, met with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi before departing for his post and outlined his proposed plan to expand bilateral cooperation between Tehran and Kampala in various fields. The foreign minister, while wishing Nourian success in his mission in Uganda, stressed the need to make use of existing capacities and opportunities to increase trade exchanges and strengthen relations and cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly in the political, economic and agricultural sectors. Before his appointment as Iran’s new ambassador to Uganda, Nourian served as deputy director of the Department for Cultural Cooperation and NGOs at the Foreign Ministry’s Center for Public Diplomacy.

item.title: Irans new ambassador in Italy meets with FM Araghchi
item.description: Ali Akbar Rezaei, the new Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran in Italy, met today, Wednesday, with Seyed Abbas Araghchi, the Minister of Foreign Affairs. During this meeting, Ali Akbar Rezaei outlined his proposed plans regarding bilateral relations between Tehran and Rome. While wishing success to Iran’s new ambassador in Rome, the Iranian Foreign Minister emphasized the importance of using all opportunities to strengthen Iran’s relations with other countries. Prior to his appointment as Iran’s new ambassador to Italy, Ali Akbar Rezaei served as Director-General of the Office of Strategic Planning and Monitoring of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Iranian Russian FMs discuss bilateral ties regional developments in Tehran
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, and Sergey Lavrov, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation, met in Tehran on Monday, October 19, 2026, and discussed the latest state of bilateral relations and the most important regional and international developments. During the meeting, the two foreign ministers reviewed the expanding relations and cooperation between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Russian Federation and emphasized the importance of continuing regular consultations between Tehran and Moscow and following up on the implementation of bilateral agreements. The two sides also exchanged views on ways to strengthen political, economic and trade cooperation and expand interactions within the framework of the Iran-Russia Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty. Regional developments, including the security situation in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, developments in Palestine and Yemen, as well as issues related to the Caucasus and Europe, were among the other topics discussed by the two foreign ministers. Araghchi and Lavrov, emphasizing the need to peacefully resolve regional disputes and crises through dialogue and political solutions, exchanged views on international developments and the need to strengthen multilateralism and cooperation in international forums. The foreign ministers of Iran and Russia also reaffirmed their countries' determination to continue close cooperation and consultation

Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to Baghdad to attend the 52nd Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), met and held talks with Fuad Hussein, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Iraq, on Sunday morning. The Iranian foreign minister expressed appreciation for Iraq’s hospitality and the excellent organization of the session, voicing hope that Iraq’s presidency of the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers would be marked by success and valuable initiatives to strengthen the organization’s standing. Referring to the need for Islamic countries to pay due attention to issues facing the Muslim world, particularly the question of Palestine and the Israeli regime’s continued expansionism and warmongering in the region, Araghchi stressed the importance of strengthening dialogue and solidarity among Muslim nations to resolve differences, enhance cohesion, and promote Islamic unity in confronting threats. During the meeting, the two sides exchanged views on Iran-Iraq relations and bilateral cooperation in various fields, particularly economic, trade, and security matters. Araghchi also briefed his Iraqi counterpart on ongoing diplomatic developments related to regional peace and security, emphasizing that the Islamic Republic of Iran, just as it remains resolute and serious in defending its national interests and security, is equally steadfast in using diplomacy to prevent an escalation of tensions and resolve issues. The Iranian foreign minister stressed that the insecurity prevailing in the Strait of Hormuz and its economic consequences for countries in the region and around the world were the direct result of the US-Zionist military aggression against Iran. Nevertheless, he noted that the Islamic Republic of Iran had declared its readiness to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz, provided the United States ceased its acts of aggression and intervention, as proposed in Iran’s seven-point plan. The foreign ministers of Iran and Iraq also exchanged views on developments in the Arabian Peninsula and ways to help bring the conflicts to an end. Referring to the need to learn lessons from developments over the past decade, Araghchi stressed that the Yemen issue could not be resolved through the use of force and a blockade. Rather, it must be addressed within the framework of the UN Charter, with respect for Yemen’s national sovereignty and territorial integrity and the human rights of its people. He reaffirmed Iran’s readiness to provide any assistance that could help facilitate dialogue between the parties. Referring to the importance of ensuring that Islamic holy sites are respected by all, Araghchi emphasized that, given the firm rejection of the claim that Yemen’s army had attacked the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, repeating this false allegation would not serve the interests of the Muslim Ummah. He added that the claim should not become a basis for division and discord within the Organization of Islamic Cooperation.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is in Baghdad to attend the 52nd Session of the Council of Foreign Ministers of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC), met and held talks with Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi on Saturday evening. During the meeting, the Iranian foreign minister expressed appreciation to the Iraqi government and people for their excellent hosting of the session, stressing the importance of making greater use of the OIC’s capacities to pursue issues concerning the Muslim world, particularly the issue of Palestine and the expansionism and warmongering of the Zionist regime. Referring to the very good relations between the two neighboring Muslim countries, Araghchi reaffirmed the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to further strengthen relations with Iraq in all areas of mutual interest. The two sides also discussed and reviewed the latest regional developments. Explaining Iran’s positions and views on peace and stability in West Asia, Araghchi stressed that the root cause of insecurity in the region is the occupation and expansionism of the Zionist regime, which, particularly over the past three years, has carried out military aggression against Lebanon, Syria, and Iran while committing genocide in Palestine, jeopardizing global peace and security. Highlighting Iran’s commitment to using diplomacy to prevent further escalation of insecurity, Araghchi recalled that it was the United States that repeatedly disrupted diplomatic processes by violating its commitments and resorting to force, thereby undermining the security of international commercial shipping. The Iranian foreign minister and the Iraqi prime minister also discussed the Saudi Arabia–Yemen conflict, ways to help end the naval blockade of Yemen, and efforts to de-escalate tensions.
